title: Scheduler Policy
description: Scheduler placement and capacity policy. The document stays open for accepted RFC 0008 dimensions, while the placement surface consumed by telemetry-informed placement — the objective, comparator, staleness and effort-order declarations, and the ordered placement rules — is validated closed. A rule declares at most one supported prefer shape; anything outside the two shapes, and any capacity key, refuses policy load rather than binding nothing.

placement.description: The placement declarations bound by capability-aware-placement@3.

objectives.description: The objective each pass is placed under. `fallback` is the explicit pass-class default; a by_pass row overrides it for one pass. A pass with neither refuses rather than defaulting silently.

comparator.description: Materiality thresholds for the unearned-effort demotion, in basis points (10000 = parity). Integers, never floats: the policy digest is taken over canonical bytes and a float threshold cannot be pinned.

staleness.description: The single definition of current evidence: a ledger distance, never a wall-clock age.

effort_order.description: The effort ladder, weakest rung first: exactly the graded efforts, each once. `default` declares that a tuple pins no effort knob and sits nowhere on the ladder, so it is not placeable here.

placement_rules.description: Ordered; first full match wins; the matched rule id enters the decision trace. Every rule states a preference or a restriction — a rule that states neither is decoration.

match.description: The closed match vocabulary. Run mode is not a placement coordinate and is not matchable here.

prefer.description: Exactly one supported shape. Two shapes name two orders and the rule then states neither; a capacity key such as expiring_capacity binds nothing and refuses.

influence.description: prefer_only reorders candidates that already survive every hard filter; it can never unlock a forbidden placement (D0008.C9).

objective.description: One of the accepted @2 placement objectives.
